When the DC power supply E=100 V acts alone, the AC voltage source set to zero is equivalent to a short circuit; in the DC steady state, inductor L is equivalent to a short circuit, and in the figure C and L are in parallel, so capacitor C is short-circuited by the inductor, and the DC voltage across the capacitor is 0 V. The image shows C and L in parallel, so ZLC = ZL || ZC = j100 Ω. This branch is in series with R = 100 Ω, so the RMS capacitor voltage is |VC| = 100·|j100|/|100+j100| = 70.7 V. method.method_draft: Let s(t) be the voltage supplied to the left side of R relative to the bottom rail, and let v(t) be the capacitor voltage. From the circuit topology, KCL at the top LC node gives (s - v)/R = C dv/dt + iL, with v = L diL/dt. Differentiate to eliminate iL: (s' - v')/R = C v'' + v/L. The DC part E has s' = 0 and, in steady state, vDC = 0 because L shorts the capacitor. For the sinusoidal part with peak source amplitude S = 100√2 and ω = 10000, use complex amplitudes: V/S = (jω/R)/(1/L - ω^2C + jω/R). Substitute R = 100 Ω, C = 1e-6 F, L = 5e-3 H: 1/L = 200, ω^2C = 100, and ω/R = 100, so |V/S| = |j100/(100+j100)| = 1/√2. Thus the capacitor peak voltage is 100√2/√2 = 100 V, so the rated voltage should be greater than 100 V.
